sections.value:
# PASS WITH NOTES — PR 277, round 2 (C34 final round)

Head: `5e700abc3e61c0ff273cc7531c5b6c77bc193a3c`.
Reviewed only the delta from `f9d2bc77871f3d7cee6418d6d18c86c26d5e40f4`;
round 1 stands for the unchanged surfaces. The review checkout is read-only.

## Round-one fixes

- **R277-1:** the client-timeout readiness trigger is reverted. Only a
  successfully returned claim ends the outage; zero-message pages already
  have that meaning in the base extension. The original independent late-401
  regression passes, along with the shipped late-401 and empty-page banner
  tests (three selected Node tests).
- **R277-2:** `restore_receiver_edges` runs once before heartbeat/reconcile
  reads the edge set, under the existing native lock. It restores only a
  seat's latest lapsed/renewed edge. Independent same-SQLite-store restart
  regression passes: exactly one outstanding lapse across restart.
- **R277-3:** an unseen pair now evicts an oldest timestamp instead of being
  suppressed at capacity; registration is never blocked. Independent
  different-seat-at-capacity regression passes. Memory
  stays bounded at 512 pairs and ping exposes a numeric eviction count.

## Requested boundary checks

The 55-second bound is checked only after an empty queue claim and during
the idle select (`delivery/mod.rs:2263-2272`), not around an in-flight queue
operation. The new deadline arm is gated by `native`; ordinary non-native
waiting keeps its old behavior. Independent paused-clock checks exercise
mail at 54.9 seconds for both ordinary and during-turn native claims, and
native/non-native idle behavior at 55 seconds.

Older extension compatibility: the final store.mjs differs from the base's
runtime logic only by a comment. Its existing successful empty-page path
validates the page, clears a prior outage, and takes the ordinary bounded
retry pause; no new wire shape or client feature is required.

**Boot read bound:** one live-Copilot roster read, then one
`latest_matching` call for each live native Copilot seat. This is not one
global SQL statement: `SqliteSpine::latest_matching` performs two
seat-and-kind-indexed `ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 1` seeks in a read snapshot,
one per edge kind (`store/spine.rs:59-65,367-394`). Thus at most two spine
rows per native seat are read, once per daemon; no whole-spine or seat-history
scan. Failures are explicitly logged as best-effort audit restoration.

## C34 follow-up R277-C34-1 — equal-time eviction ties

`crates/daemon/src/registration/refusals.rs:54-58`

Eviction is oldest-first when timestamps differ, but **not deterministic
among equal timestamps**: `min_by_key` orders only by the Instant and
HashMap iteration breaks ties. The existing test gives each entry a distinct
millisecond and cannot show that. An isolated equal-time probe records
13 distinct victims across 16 identically populated independent windows.

This is a nonblocking **C34 follow-up**, not another review round: all tied
candidates are equally old, unseen pairs are still told, the count is right,
and no registration decision depends on which tied pair is evicted. If a
deterministic tie is wanted, use the pair as a secondary ordering key and
add one equal-time test.

## Security delta

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| — | — | Reviewed delta | — | No security vulnerabilities found under C33 | — |

The scoped security review found no new vulnerabilities. Invalid/refused
claims still reach identity/registration checks before the new idle wait;
silence and 4xx responses cannot trigger the client's ready event. Restore
queries use the mandatory row seat and exactly the two native receiver
edge kinds, not a payload-supplied seat or unrelated events.
`refusals_evicted` is a u64 counter; no seat, refusal body, credentials or
environment text was added to that field. Advice-only restart behavior is
unchanged from round 1.

## Cost

The new in-process idle deadline rides the existing long-poll select; it
launches no process and adds no polling loop. The ordinary 500-ms native
revalidation wake is unchanged. An idle client now repeats a claim after
55 seconds plus its existing retry pause (up to 5 seconds), rather than a
65-second client timeout plus that pause: approximately one request per
60 versus 70 seconds per continuously idle native seat at steady backoff.
Boot restoration scales with current native seats, not spine history; the
window's retain/eviction work remains bounded by 512 entries per refusal.
Live before/after deployment receipts remain with the separate performance
verdict; this review did not deploy or bounce anything.

## Validation

- `just pr-freeze 277`: FINAL at the full reviewed head; five CI checks pass.
- `just copilot-native-test`: PASS, 364 passed / 3 skipped.
- In the isolated exact-head archive:
  `nice -n 19 node --test --test-name-pattern='review: a late refused claim|R277-1:|an idle seat.s banner clears' .copilot/extensions/pij/store.test.mjs`:
  PASS, three tests including the unchanged independent round-one fixture.
- `harness boot --json`: advisory NOT-READY (no local node_modules).
- `harness checks --json`: exit 1. Native contracts, Copilot SDK, route
  inventory, smoke and pij-skill PASS. Eight TS/tooling-dependent stages
  fail in this dependency-free worktree (tsx/vitest unavailable and ambient
  Biome incompatible); attribution warns for missing tsx.
  The Rust stage exits 101 in the unchanged `pij-tmux --test adapter` suite.
  Per pm-001's explicit direction, that is the separately owned F228 work,
  out of scope for this delta; the queued adapter rerun was canceled and
  is not a completion condition here. This is not a claimed green full gate.
- Isolated exact-head archive:
  `just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-daemon --lib review_ -- --nocapture`:
  PASS, 10 selected tests including both unchanged original SQLite/capacity
  regressions and the new 54.9-second ordinary/during-turn and native/non-native
  boundary checks. The SQLite restart log contains one lapsed edge.
- `just shared-build -- test --locked -p pij-daemon --lib an_idle_native_claim_is_answered_empty_at_the_daemons_bound -- --nocapture`:
  PASS, the shipped daemon-side idle-answer contract.
- `just shared-build -- test --offline --manifest-path d2-proof/Cargo.toml -- --nocapture`:
  PASS, five tests: the three shipped window tests, original capacity
  regression and equal-time eviction probe. This additional dependency-free
  window replay substitutes std Instant for Tokio Instant only; the original
  capacity regression above also passes against the unadapted daemon module.
- All Rust proof used the canonical shared target lock, niceness 19,
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 and four jobs. Added fixtures are confined to the
  session archive; no reviewed product files changed.

No mutation-count claim is needed for this round. The linked author receipt
lists R1-M2 as SURVIVED, so I did not treat the summary's six mutations as six
caught faults; requested regression results are independently recorded here.

## Harness feedback

magicWand: retain a dependency-free exact-head regression replay recipe.
The three round-one fixtures are reusable without rewriting them; the
isolated replay adds only the specifically requested 54.9/55-second checks.
The equal-time probe is the concrete fixture to promote with the C34
follow-up. The harness failure envelope retained only stderr's tail and
lost the adapter test assertion on stdout; preserving the two streams
together would avoid an unnecessary diagnostic rerun. No product or
governance file was hand-edited.
